summary: Intercompany payout job stalled due to stale bank-account revocation flag on merged vendor profile
description:
Issue summary:
An automated intercompany payout sweep scheduled for 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC did not complete. Multiple vendor payout batches stayed in status 'pending_review' and the settlement scheduler marked the run as 'hung'. Finance Ops observed missing disbursements for three internal vendor profiles that share merged identifiers.

Impact:
- Netting and cash-position reports were understated for the AP entity (EMEA).
- Affects 3 scheduled intercompany disbursements totaling $482,190.
- Downstream bank files not generated; reconciliations delayed for EMEA payroll vendor.

Context / background:
We recently executed a vendor-merge to consolidate duplicate vendor records for a long-standing supplier (internal intercompany payee). The merge created a single canonical vendor_id with legacy sub-ids preserved. Finance Ops raised a support ticket when the scheduled settlement did not push to the bank gateway.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger the intercompany payout sweep for date 2026-03-10 in prod (settlements-scheduler v2).
2) Check vendor_status table for canonical vendor_id 773-EMEA-MERGE.
3) Observe bank_account.revoke_flag==true on the merged profile even though individual legacy accounts are active.
4) Settlement job marks batch as pending_review due to 'bank-account-revoked' guardrail.
logs_and_errors:
2026-03-10T02:00:03Z scheduler[settlements]: starting sweep run id=run-20260310-02
2026-03-10T02:00:05Z payouts[worker-7]: evaluating vendor=773-EMEA-MERGE sub_ids=[773a,773b,773c]
2026-03-10T02:00:05Z payouts[worker-7]: WARNING: vendor-bank-check failed: bank_account.revoke_flag=true (bank_id=GB99BANK000123)
2026-03-10T02:00:06Z payouts[worker-7]: batch=run-20260310-02 vendor=773 status=pending_review reason="revoked bank flag"
2026-03-10T02:00:06Z scheduler[settlements]: run run-20260310-02 set status=hung because all live items require manual review
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: vendor-merge logic inherited a stale 'revoke_flag' from a legacy sub-account that had been closed previously.
Findings to date:
- vendor_merged_view shows revoke_flag=true on canonical bank_account record, but 'bank_account_history' shows last update was in 2024-11 during a cleanup migration. No recent delta from Finance Ops.
- The payments microservice validates canonical.bank_account.revoke_flag before generating bank files; it does not re-check sub_id tuples.
- There is a race in the vendor-merge job where the historical revoke flag is copied into canonical without reconciling active_sub_accounts.
- Related protective guardrail introduced in PR github.com/redwood/payments/pull/4123 intentionally blocks any vendor with revoke_flag to avoid accidental payouts to stale accounts. This is working as designed but surfaced due to bad merge state.
Next steps:
- Manual: clear revoke_flag for canonical after verifying active sub-accounts (Finance Ops + Payments Eng).
- Medium-term: patch vendor-merge to compute canonical.revoke_flag = AND(all_sub_accounts.revoke_flag==true) instead of OR semantics.
- Add unit test covering vendor-merge behavior for bank flags and writeback.

resolution: Workaround applied: cleared stale revoke_flag on canonical vendor after manual verification of active sub-accounts, retried the sweep, and bank files were generated. Root cause: vendor-merge logic copied legacy revoke state into canonical record (OR semantics) which blocked automated payouts. Follow-up: deploy merge-fix PR (github.com/redwood/payments/pull/4156), add audit check in Finance Ops runbook to validate canonical bank flags after merges, and add a monitoring alert for 'sweep hung due to pending_review' to avoid silent failures.
